metadata.title: OMODA: Orchestrated Multi-model Operator with Delegated Autonomy

content_summary: OMODA agent-capability PRD. Thesis: human-gating every dangerous action is a workaround for absent enforced containment; NVIDIA OpenShell supplies the enforcement (Landlock FS, deny-by-default L7 egress, dropped caps, gateway credential brokering), so OMODA moves the human gate from the ACTION to the ENVELOPE: approve a policy delta once, every later use of that capability is autonomous. Deliberate inverse of prior art the8genc/chief-of-staff (agents.getonpace.org), whose sendGate.js gates every send; OMODA keeps the single-choke-point pattern generalized as the Autonomy Broker. Tiers: T0 contained -> silent execute; T1 irreversible-but-in-envelope -> register inverse first, execute, Telegram UNDO (30min TTL); T2 boundary-crossing -> OpenShell already denied, escalate the exact policy delta, APPROVE applies it and retries; T3 prohibited -> no approval path in code. T3 self-protection clause is the highest-severity rule: refuse deltas that weaken OpenShell itself (disable managed_inference, add an inference host directly to network policy, disable device auth, apply personal-open-internet); without it T2 is a privilege-escalation ladder. Three models: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning hosted via gateway (planner), Nemotron 3 Nano Omni local vLLM :8000 (perception + risk classifier, zero egress for sensitive data), <=3B guard model memory-gated. Verified box state, risk register (R1 no telegram preset, R2 HERMES availability, R3 unknown port block, R7 unreadable Notion page), compliance table pinning every dep to a version published on/before 2026-08-01, and headline metric G1 (>=10x reduction in human approvals vs a per-action-gated control run).
